widgets_values: Street-style portrait of a young woman with shoulder-length dark hair, wearing a camel trench coat and a cream knit scarf, walking along a sunlit autumn boulevard lined with golden trees and Parisian cafes. Golden hour backlight, warm tones, 85mm lens, shallow depth of field, editorial fashion photography, photorealistic.

Change the scene in @Image1 to a snowy night in a Tokyo street: falling snow, glowing neon signs in pink and cyan reflected on the wet pavement, snowflakes caught in her hair and on her coat. Keep the same woman, her face, pose, outfit and framing. Cinematic night photography, photorealistic.

## AMD MiniMax H3 Image Edit

Requires a **personal** account key: the shared key is refused with a permission error for this model. Register at https://h3.oneclickamd.ai/?utm_source=comfyui, then save it to `h3_gateway_api_key.txt` in the ComfyUI user directory. **One-time setup per machine** — it applies to every workflow.

The same key also works for the AMD MiniMax H3 video and AMD Qwen Image 2.1 nodes, so configure it once.

**On the Windows Desktop app**, the file belongs in Desktop's install directory, for example `C:\Users\<you>\AppData\Local\Comfy-Desktop\ComfyUI-Installs\ComfyUI\ComfyUI\user\h3_gateway_api_key.txt`. Make it with Notepad: the default encoding is right, and **New > Text Document** already ends in `.txt`.

If the key is missing, the node fails immediately and tells you the registration URL and the exact file path, so you never sit through a silent 401.

**Your key is not in this workflow.** The node has no `api_key` widget, so the key is never written into the workflow JSON or embedded into exported image metadata. This workflow is safe to share.

**How it works:** the first node generates a street portrait, and the second node restages it as a snowy neon night, referring to it in the prompt as `@Image1`. To edit your own photo, replace the first node with a **Load Image** node.

**Parameters:** connect 1 to 3 reference images and the node edits or combines them, referred to as `@Image1`, `@Image2` and `@Image3` in connection order. `aspect_ratio` sets the output shape; an edit is reframed to it. When editing an image you generated, use a different `seed` from the one that made it, as this workflow does. Each image costs 4 credits, so one run of this workflow costs 8.
